title: Behavioral task specification, v1
description: THE frozen artifact. Everything downstream is a function of this file.
A task is four epoch bands in order -- engagement, stimulus sampling, response,
outcome -- with four INDEPENDENT layers of parameterization. Only layer 1
(topology) changes the graph; layers 2-4 are tables bound to a fixed graph.
That split is the whole point: a reversal is a layer-2 edit, an eased variant is a
layer-3 edit, and neither moves a single node.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: there is no `nodes` key and no `edges` key. Nodes are
emitted by versioned epoch templates in templates/, never authored per task. Arbitrary
graphs are not supported, and that constraint is what makes compilation, validation and
the eventual UI tractable. See docs/decisions.md D1.
VERSIONING: spec_version is frozen from day one and travels with every compiled table,
so a recorded session can always be reconstructed against the schema that produced it.

spec_version.description: Schema version. Travels with the compiled table into the session record.

spec_id.description: Stable identity. Used in the spec hash and in provenance; renaming one splits its history, exactly as renaming a task.json profile would.

vocab_version.description: Which strobe_vocab.vN.json this spec was authored against. Separate from spec_version because the vocabulary grows (append-only) far more often than the schema changes.

meta.description: Human provenance. Never affects compilation, but IS covered by the spec hash, so an edit here is visible in the session record.

reproduces_sketch.description: Path to the firmware sketch this spec must reproduce bit-identically, if any. Absence means the task is novel and has no equivalence target.

derived_from.description: spec_id this was forked from. Set on variants that are a pure layer-3 delta (e.g. an _EZ), so the claim is checkable rather than asserted.

topology.description: LAYER 1 -- the only layer that changes the graph.

timing.description: LAYER 3 -- one duration per node, addressed by id.

contingency.description: LAYER 2 -- per trial. Reversals live entirely here.

policy.description: LAYER 4 -- orthogonal. Hooks onto selection and terminals only.

description: A strobe is one of: a NAME resolved against the append-only vocabulary; a @binding
resolved from the trial at selection time; or null.
null is legal and explicit. Current firmware emits nothing at all when the response
window expires (BehaviorBox.h:1090-1091), and grgl_2odor must reproduce that silence
to pass the equivalence gate. The linter warns on null rather than erroring, and the
warning must say when the silence is deliberate. See docs/decisions.md D4.

timingRef.description: An id declared in the timing vector. NEVER a literal duration -- that is what makes a shaping ramp a table rewrite rather than a recompile.

template.description: Which versioned epoch template in templates/ emits the node and edge lists.

template_version.description: Pinned so a template edit cannot silently change an existing task's graph. A bump requires re-validating the affected specs.

n_sampling_stages.description: Stimuli presented per trial, in sequence. Unrolls the sampling band; >1 requires per-stage bindings in contingency.trial_types[].stages. 0 is legal for a task with no stimulus (pure timing/shaping).

retention_delay.description: Insert an unfilled DELAY between sampling and the response window.

description: n_alternative: entry into the target port advances toward reward, entry
elsewhere is an error, expiry is an omission.
go_nogo: success is defined by INACTION -- expiry is correct and any entry is
a false alarm.
The interpreter never branches on this field. Both modes are expressed by which
outcome classes carry which edge effects, so 'correct = timeout' needs no special
case. See docs/decisions.md D9.

response_ports.description: Input channels live in the response window. n-alternative scaling costs one edge each out of a single WAIT_ENTRY.

commit_hold.description: Require a sustained hold to initiate. When true the graph gains a HOLD between the engagement window and the first stimulus, so a broken hold costs no stimulus presentation.

description: Where the LIGHTS_OFF node sits relative to the behavioural strobe it accompanies.
This exists because current firmware is INCONSISTENT: LIGHTS_OFF precedes its
partner on all three abort paths (BehaviorBox.h:1158-1159, :1180-1181, :1196-1197)
but FOLLOWS it on the success path (:1210 then :1213). Reproducing GRGL
bit-identically requires expressing that flip, so it is a declared field rather
than a hidden template constant. See docs/decisions.md D2.
LAYER 3. An ORDERED list; a node's duration is an id here, which the compiler
resolves to an index. Order is load-bearing: the index is what the firmware holds,
and a stage ramp rewrites entries in place by index.
Generalises applyStage() (BehaviorBox.h:567-574), which already rewrites a small
mutable vector the trial loop indexes -- from 4 entries to N.

ms.description: uint16. Firmware stores timings as signed int (max 32767) AND uses 32767 as the StageStep 'never' sentinel (BehaviorBox.h:531-536), so a legal duration collides with a sentinel. uint16 doubles the range and removes the collision -- a deliberate, documented divergence. See docs/decisions.md D6.

wire_key.description: The legacy START-line token that supplies this value, if any. The mapping is MANY-TO-ONE: odorPokeHold (S0P) drives both the commitment hold and the sampling hold (BehaviorBox.h:1176, :1191), so two ids may declare the same wire_key. See docs/decisions.md D8.

contingency.description: LAYER 2. Everything that varies per trial. A reversal is entirely a context_schedule edit -- no state, edge or duration moves.

stimuli.description: Emitter channel plus identity code per stimulus. 'Stimulus' is an emitter channel and nothing more, so a speaker or LED substitutes for an odor valve with no interpreter change.

emitter.description: Actuator channel name resolved against the box pinout.

ports.description: Per-channel bindings. Indexed at runtime by $ch (the channel that fired), which is what lets one branch node serve every port instead of one node per port. See docs/decisions.md D3.

trial_types.description: The trial pool. Mirrors firmware's TrialType (BehaviorBox.h:169-184) so the equivalence gate compares like with like.

stages.description: Stimulus id per sampling stage, in order. Length MUST equal topology.n_sampling_stages. Referenced from a node as @stim[$stage].on_code, which is what makes a sequence task an unroll rather than a rewrite.

target.description: Correct port, or null on a withhold trial. Resolved as @target.

weight.description: Relative frequency for weighted-pool selection. Ignored where selection is live (anti-bias).

description: Block boundaries that swap targets. THIS IS WHERE REVERSALS LIVE, in full.
An empty list is a single-block task. Adding an entry re-maps stimulus->port
without moving any node, so strobe structure stays comparable across blocks --
which is the property that makes within-subject reversal analysis valid.

targets.description: trial_type id -> target port, overriding the trial_types default from this trial count on.

description: Response class -> what it earns and where it terminates.
A spec declares ONLY the classes its topology can produce; the linter checks the
set against the template. go_nogo declares correct+false_alarm and has no
omission or hold_fail, because there is no response hold to break.
Reward/consumption states are emitted by the PRESENCE of a reward binding. A
null reward removes the PULSE and WAIT_EXIT from that branch -- absence, not a
suppressing flag.

channel.description: Input channel name resolved against the box pinout.

reward_duration.description: Pulse width = delivered volume. An index, so a ramp can change reward size mid-session.

description: TRIAL_CORRECT advances and clears penalty escalation. TRIAL_INCORRECT advances
(unless a correction budget repeats it). TRIAL_INVALID repeats without advancing
-- used where the trial carries no evidence about discrimination, so an unsampled
trial never enters the behavioural record as a choice.

reward.description: '@target' to reward the chosen port, a port id for a fixed line, or null for none. Null omits the reward PULSE and consumption WAIT_EXIT from this branch entirely.

strobe.description: Entry strobe of this branch's penalty/terminal node. Explicitly null where firmware is silent.

description: Which trigger routes here. Naming it makes 'correct = TIMEOUT' on a go/no-go
withhold window a declaration rather than a special case.
NAMED `trigger`, NOT `on`: YAML 1.1 resolves a bare `on` key to the boolean
true, so `on: TIMEOUT` silently becomes `true: TIMEOUT` and the field vanishes.
Hand-authoring the specs caught this; a generated spec would have hidden it
until the compiler read a key that was not there. `trigger` also matches the
edge vocabulary the model already uses. See docs/decisions.md D12.
LAYER 4. Hooks onto trial selection and terminals ONLY -- never onto the middle of
a trial. An absent block means defined default behaviour, never an error, mirroring
firmware's TrialPolicy where a nullptr means legacy semantics (BehaviorBox.h:1010-1015).

bias_window.description: Max 32: BEHAVIOR_MAX_BIAS_WINDOW (BehaviorBox.h:463). The ring is statically sized at 32 regardless of the configured window, so this is a hard ceiling, not a suggestion.

max_run.description: Hard cap on consecutive identical correct sides. With p_min/p_max it stops selection collapsing into a deterministic -- and therefore cueable -- pattern.

correction.description: Per-side leading correction budgets. Consumed by advancing trials on that side; an under-budget error repeats the same side WITHOUT consuming budget. 0/0 means never repeat, which is legacy bare-START behaviour.

applies_to.description: Which outcome class escalates. Only the no-engagement penalty escalates today.

description: MUST be declared, never implied. BehaviorBox.h:1171-1174: 'the abstention
escalator is NOT reset here. A bare odor-poke (or a poke-and-bail) must not
defuse the lazy penalty -- only a completed CORRECT trial clears it... This
closes the poke-to-reset loophole, which the old EZ copy of this loop had
reopened.'
That is a past failure mode, closed once in C++, and reopened once already by
a copy-paste. Making it a required declared field is how it stays closed.

arm_after_stage.description: Escalation arms once this stage row is live. An eased task points this at its last row so an animal still being shaped is never escalated against.

description: LAYER 3 REWRITES, scheduled by trial count. This is the mechanism the whole
layer-3 claim rests on: an eased variant of a task is THIS BLOCK and nothing
else, which is directly checkable by diffing two specs.
Rows are scanned descending with >=, so the schedule is idempotent -- applying it
twice, or skipping a count, lands on the same row. The switch-on-exact-index it
replaces fired once and only if the counter hit that value precisely
(BehaviorBox.h:551-562). An unreachable row is expressed by OMITTING it, not by
a sentinel trial count.

set.description: timing id -> new ms. Addressed by id, resolved to index at compile time, so the firmware rewrite is a memcpy into the timing vector.

description: 'host' means the host draws it from a CSPRNG and sends it on the START line; the
board echoes it back and BOTH values are recorded, so a board still running old
firmware that seeds itself is detectable (Ephymeris runner.py:66-74).
A literal integer is for reproducing a specific session and should never be
committed on a production spec. Seeding happens exactly once per run: two seeding
sites is how a fixed seed creeps back in unnoticed, which is what made the shaping
sketches run an identical trial sequence every session forever
(BehaviorBox.h:203-209).
